newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - APP prices, others on outlook.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - APP prices, others on outlook.

text.p: Asian debt markets drifted to a slow close on Friday, but there were a few developments of note.
Peregrine Fixed Income announced that the floating rate note issue for APP Global Finance III had been priced and increased.
The five-year notes were priced at 425 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate, toward the wide end of the 400-425 basis point indicated price range.
The size of the issue was raised to US$500 million from US$400 million at the deal's launch in mid-March. Syndication will close on Monday.
On the loan side, Indonesia's PT Gajah Surya Finance set a US$40 million two-tranche loan.
From Hong Kong came news that two Hong Kong dollar issues had been increased.

Shanghai Commercial Bank's floating rate certificate of deposit issue was raised to HK$680 million from HK$600 million, while Chekiang First Bank's FRCD was boosted to HK$1.25 billion from HK$1.0 billion at launch.
Next week offers some hefty deals, bankers said.

The Yankee bond for Kingdom of Thailand is expected to launch via lead managers Lehman Brothers and Salomon Brothers. The bond will start off at US$500 milion and is expected to have a 10-year and possibly a 30-year tranche.
Bank of China may also be in the market with its US$200-$300 million floating rate note issue to be launched via Morgan Stanley International.
The issue will have a maturity of five or seven years, the lead manager said. Bankers are betting on a five-year tenor.
If the FRN is indeed five-years, it is likely to pay a slightly tighter spread than China Construction Bank, which offered 37.5 basis points all-in for its five-year paper launched earlier this week.
In other news from debt markets, the Asian Development Bank is seen launching a US$1.0 billion 10-year global bond as soon as market conditions allow, traders said.
